summary: Bunzaburo Matsumoto specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz (~1890–1893). His career included professorships at Rikkyo University (1894), First Higher School (~1899–1906), and Kyoto University, where he was president (1908–1915).

Burchard Brentjes worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1947–1952) under Heinz Mode (~1948–1954), later serving there on faculty (~1954–1978) and succeeding Mode in 1978.

Burkard Wilhelm Leist was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Göttingen (~1837–1841), Heidelberg, and Berlin under Friedrich Carl von Savigny (~1840–1841). He was professor of law at Basel (1846), Rostock (1847), and Jena (1853).

Burkhard Quessel specializes in Tibetology and Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was a member (attested 1996–1997), and later served as curator at the British Library (attested 1999–2012).

Burmansah Burmansah focuses on Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a bachelor's degree at Universitas Komputer Indonesia (2004–2008) and a master's at the State University of Jakarta (2014–2016). He was appointed lecturer at STIAB Jinarakkhita in 2020.
Burt Thorp, who studied under Hartmut Scharfe, worked in Indology. He held a post at the University of North Dakota (attested 1998–1999).

Burton Stein was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Illinois Chicago and the University of Chicago (~1950–1954). He held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–1983) and SOAS University of London (1983).

Burton Watson was a scholar of Sinology and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Kyoto University. He taught at Doshisha University (~1951–1952), Columbia (1961), and Stanford (~1964–1965).

Byambyn Rinchen was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the Leningrad Orient Institute (~1924–1927) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1956–1957), and held a post at the National University of Mongolia.
Byung-gon Kim specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied abroad at Rissho University (attested 2007) and serves as professor, dean, and institute director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

C. C. Berg was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under G. A. J. Hazeu and Nicolaas Johannes Krom (~1922–1927) and served as Professor of Javanese there from 1929 to 1972.

C. Collin Davies worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Aberystwyth University (~1919–1922) and Peterhouse, Cambridge (~1922–1926). He served as Lecturer in Indian History at SOAS (1926–1936) and Reader at Oxford (1936–1963).

C. D. Sebastian works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, studied under Abhimanyu Singh and Ashok Kumar Chatterjee, and held a post as Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

C. Kunhan Raja worked in Indology and philosophy, earning a D.Phil. at Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He became the first University Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (1927) and honorary director of the Adyar Library (attested 1928–1938).

C. M. Naim worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1959–1961) and served on the faculty at the University of Chicago from around 1961 to 2001, becoming Professor Emeritus.

C. M. Ridding studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Girton College and the University of Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell and T. W. Rhys Davids. She held positions cataloguing at Girton College (1904) and as librarian at Cambridge University Library (1911).
C. Peter Bankart, a scholar in Buddhist studies, served as a visiting researcher at Dartmouth College and held a post at Wabash College (attested 2003).

C. Pierce Salguero works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University. He held positions at the University of Pennsylvania (2011–2012) and Pennsylvania State University (from 2010).
C. R. Krishnamacharlu was an Indologist and historian who studied at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College. He held a post at the Archaeological Survey of India from around 1911 to 1943.
C. S. Srinivasachariar was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).
